newsitem.title: TURKEY: US urges Kurd groups to implement ceasefire.
newsitem.headline: US urges Kurd groups to implement ceasefire.

text.p: U.S. envoy Robert Pelletreau on Wednesday urged warring Iraqi factions to implement a ceasefire to end two months of fighting that has hurt Washington's anti-Baghdad policy.

"We have agreed on the desirability of ending the fighting...Turkey, the United States and the United Kingdom now call on both sides to implement this ceasefire in place beginning immediately," Pelletreau said in a statement.

Pelletreau said that in two days of talks in Turkey he had reached agreement in principle with Massoud Barzani, leader of the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) and Jalal Talabani of the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) on a U.S.-sponsored truce.
"Each side will take defensive positions and not initiate firing or hostilities," said Pelletreau, U.S. assistant secretary of state for near eastern affairs.
Further meetings with delegations from each group were planned in Ankara next week with representatives of the United States, Britain and Turkey, he said.
But there were reports of skirmishes in the region hours after Pelletreau concluded his meetings late on Tuesday.

"The PUK started fighting just two hours after the talks," said KDP Ankara representative Faik Nerweyi told Reuters, adding that Talabani was getting help from Iran. The PUK, which denies any help from Tehran, was not immediately available for comment.
The sporadic fighting between the rival factions worsened on August 31 when Barzani got backing from Baghdad to take the main north Iraqi city of Arbil, which had been in PUK hands since late 1994.
